headline: A hacker tested Bitget's defenses with a tiny transfer, then stole $388 million in just over an hour

sources.title: Bitget Says Attacker Exploited Third-Party Security Product Flaw to Steal $388M
Bitget attacker tested risk controls with small transfers before $388 million theft, CEO says

summary: On 24 September 2026, an attacker who had gained high-level access through a zero-day flaw in a third-party security product sent two tiny "probe" transfers (0.184 ETH, 193 TRX) from Bitget's wallets, small enough to stay under automated risk-alarm thresholds. Neither tripped an alert. The attacker then drained roughly $361 million across 17 transactions on 8 blockchains over about 71 minutes (6:58–8:09pm UTC); total losses reached $388 million from hot and warm wallets. Bitget's own systems flagged a discrepancy just 7 minutes after the large transfers began — not fast enough to stop the theft. Cold wallets and customer balances were unaffected (covered by Bitget's $464M+ User Protection Fund). Bitget suspects North Korea-linked hackers; this is the exchange's own attribution, not confirmed by any law-enforcement body, and no individual has been named or charged.
